newsitem.title: INDIA: Good import arrivals ease India sunflower prices.
newsitem.headline: Good import arrivals ease India sunflower prices.

text.p: Sunflower oil prices eased by about 500 rupees ($14) per tonne in domestic markets during the past week while prices of other edible oils remained steady, industry officials said on Wednesday.

They said crude sunflower oil was currently quoted at 26,000 rupees per tonne compared to 26,500 rupees per tonne last week. Sunflower oil prices fell following steady import arrivals from the United States and Argentina.
"Except sunflower oil, all other oils were steady," Navinbhai Shah, president of Bombay Oilseeds and Oil Exchange Ltd, told Reuters.
Industry officials and traders said India had so far contracted to import 150,000 tonnes of sunflower oil of which 50,000 tonnes had already arrived.
"Another ship from the United States with 15,000 tonnes of sunflower was currently being unloaded," Shah said.
Traders said groundnut was quoted at around 34,000 rupees per tonne and palm olein was quoted at 28,000 rupees per tonne, the same as last week.

Shah said small quantities of oilseeds from the summer crop had started arriving in the domestic markets. The summer crop harvest starts from March. The Agriculture Ministry has set an output target of 9.5 million tonnes of summer oilseeds.
India harvests two oilseed crops annually, with the bulk of its output from the winter crop. The winter crop is sown in July and harvest starts from October.
